title: [grug] Launch the QuACK grouped GEMMs without PDL
body:
The three QuACK grouped-GEMM launchers in `quack_moe_cute` now pass `use_pdl=False`, so the gated, plain, and weight-gradient kernels start after the preceding kernel completes instead of overlapping it under programmatic dependent launch.

QuACK 0.6.4's SM100 GEMM executes `griddepcontrol.wait` only in its TMA-load and CLC-scheduler warps. The MMA and epilogue warps decode their work tiles from `cu_seqlens` in global memory before any wait, so a PDL-launched GEMM can read the expert group boundaries before the previous kernel's writes are visible. Both GPU dumps of the ragged EP hero hang (#8870, steps 107501 and 108711) show that split: in every stuck CTA the MMA and epilogue warps retired on a tile the load and scheduler warps still held as valid, and one cluster retired on its first tile. The load warp then blocks on the A/B pipeline and the rank never reaches the next ragged all-to-all barrier.

Cost was measured on the six-GEMM expert MLP forward and backward at the hero shape (601,088 rows, 6 experts, hidden 6144, intermediate 3072) on two GB200 nodes, 1,000 iterations per arm, each arm twice per GPU: median 87.6 ms per iteration with PDL off against 87.7 ms with PDL on on one node, 88.7 ms against 88.5 ms on the other, within 0.3% and inside the per-GPU spread. 32,000 iterations ran without a hang or non-finite value.

The change is a mitigation. Neither probe reproduced the hang in 100,000 launches, and the hero rate is about one hang per 1e6 GPU-steps, so the change is judged by the recurrence interval on the next hero relaunch. The probes and their per-arm results are recorded on the issue. The upstream fix is a `griddepcontrol.wait` in QuACK's MMA and epilogue warps, which one probe arm exercised with a patched copy of QuACK.

Part of #8870
